text.p: Britons spent 13.9 billion stg on domestic business and holiday trips in 1996, an increase of nine percent, the English Tourist Board (ETB) said on Thursday.
Revenue from domestic tourism in England rose seven percent to 10.7 billion stg, the ETB said in its annual report.
ETB chairman David Quarmby noted that the total number of holiday nights spent in England was basically static and urged greater efforts to promote tourism in the face of competition from abroad.
"For us to remain competitive in the world tourism market, more needs to be done to raise the profile of England as a good-value destination," he said.
"We need to ensure that consistently high quality is delivered by the industry to visitors," he added in a statement.
Total tourism turnover in the UK amounts to some 40 billion stg annually, more than five percent of GDP.
